parties: Plaintiff: Hang Yick Properties Management Limited
Defendant: The Incorporated Owners of Kam Fung Building, Yuen Long

facts.F1: The Plaintiff was appointed as the building manager of Kam Fung Building at Castle Peak Road, Yuen Long in 1988.
facts.F2: The Plaintiff's appointment was terminated in October 1994.
facts.F3: The Plaintiff claims to have incurred and accumulated a deficit of HK$267,540.07 between 1989 and October 1994.
facts.F4: The Defendant is the Incorporated owners of Kam Fung Building.
facts.F5: The Defendant alleges that the Plaintiff has breached the terms and conditions of the deed of mutual covenant.
facts.F6: The Plaintiff failed to deliver all books and accounts to the Defendant or the owners of the building.
facts.F7: The Plaintiff did not provide an accurate summary of all items of income and expenditure for the management of the building.
facts.F8: The Plaintiff did not report on the balance sheet as at the date of termination of the appointment of the manager.
facts.F9: The Defendant alleges that the Plaintiff's claimed expenses were not wholly, exclusively or properly incurred in the management of the building.
facts.F10: The trial of the action is scheduled to start on 21 June 2000 and end on 23 June 2000.
facts.F11: The Defendant complained that the vouchers, invoices, and other accounting documents for the period from February 1988 to June 1991 ('pre-1991') were not discovered by the Plaintiff until Thursday, 18 May 2000.
facts.F12: The Plaintiff's former solicitors had claimed that these documents were not in the Plaintiff's possession, but they were in fact possessed by the Plaintiff.
facts.F13: The Defendant is asking for the trial date to be vacated to deal with the recently discovered documents.
facts.F14: The Defendant took out another application to adjourn the trial fixed for 21 June 2000.
facts.F15: The Plaintiff argues that the late disclosure of the 'pre-1991' accounting documents has been corrected by the further discovery made on 18 May 2000.
facts.F16: The Plaintiff adduced evidence that there ought to be ample time for the Defendant to produce an accounting report by 21 June 2000.
facts.F17: The Defendant had an opportunity to compile an accountant's report by 21 June 2000 if it proceeds with due diligence after the discovery of the 'pre-1991' accounting documents.

facts.F1: The registered owner of a property in Repulse Bay entered into a Provisional Sale and Purchase Agreement ('the 1st Provisional Sale and Purchase Agreement') to sell the property to the Defendant on 2 November 1997.
facts.F2: The purchase price was $22m.  The agreement was delivered on 8 January 1998 for registration at the Land Registry.
facts.F3: It had not been registered by the Land Registry by 19 March 1998.
facts.F4: In early March 1998, the Plaintiff became interested in the property and instructed its agent to conduct a land search which showed the date, the parties and the consideration in respect of the 1st Provisional Sale and Purchase Agreement.
facts.F5: The Plaintiff assumed that the 1st Provisional Sale and Purchase, like most provisional agreements, contained 'escape clauses' whereby the parties are given 'an option to back out'.
facts.F6: The Purchaser signed a Provisional Sale and Purchase Agreement ('the 2nd Provisional Sale and Purchase Agreement') offering to purchase the property for $20.58m on 7 March 1998.
facts.F7: The escape clauses in this agreement were deleted and the Purchaser drew a cheque for $700,000 as initial deposit.
facts.F8: On 12 March 1998, the Purchaser's solicitors told the Purchaser that the Confirmor's solicitors had said that no formal Agreement had yet been signed between the registered owner and the Confirmor.
facts.F9: On 14 March 1998, the Purchaser's solicitors wrote to the Confirmor's solicitors asking for the 1st Provisional Sale and Purchase Agreement 'as soon as possible'.
facts.F10: On 16 March 1998, the Purchaser's solicitors wrote a letter asserting the existence of the contract and propounding rights under it.
facts.F11: The Purchaser did not rescind, nor was it intending or considering rescission of, the 2nd Provisional Sale and Purchase Agreement on the ground of misrepresentation.
facts.F12: On 16 March 1998, the Purchaser's solicitors wrote a letter which led to the Purchaser's issue of the writ.
facts.F13: The letter of 16 March 1998 was an unequivocal election by the Purchaser to affirm the contract.
facts.F14: There are no serious material factual disputes in the present case.
facts.F15: The Confirmor did not have any obligation to deduce title at that stage.

requested_remedy: summary judgment for wrongful repudiation of agreements for sale and purchase of properties
parties: Defendant: ['New Asia Associates (HK) Limited', 'Sky Fox Investment Limited']

facts.F1: The Plaintiff purchased two properties, namely the 31st and 32nd floors of Billion Plaza, No. 8 Cheung Yue Street, Cheung Sha Wan, Kowloon, Hong Kong.
facts.F2: New Asia Associates (HK) Limited is the vendor of the 31st floor, while Sky Fox Investment Limited is the vendor of the 32nd floor.
facts.F3: The agreements for sale and purchase were both dated 22 July 2008 with a purchase price of $40 million for each property and a deposit of $20 million payable for each property.
facts.F4: The completion date for both properties was stated as 22 October 2008 with a provision to make time of the essence of the performance of the agreement.
facts.F5: The deposits were paid by the Plaintiff on 22 July 2008.
facts.F6: During the investigation of title, requisitions were raised by the Plaintiff's solicitors leading to negotiations for a downward adjustment of the purchase price.
facts.F7: On 21 August 2008, supplemental agreements were entered into reducing the purchase price for each property from $40 million to $37.5 million.
facts.F8: Provisional liquidators were appointed for U-Right International Holdings Limited, the ultimate holding company of the Defendants on 6 October 2008.
facts.F9: The provisional liquidators wrote to the Plaintiff's solicitors on 20 October 2008 stating that they took control of the affairs of the Defendants and desired to investigate the transactions.
facts.F10: The provisional liquidators indicated that the Defendants would not proceed with the completion of the transactions on 22 October 2008.
facts.F11: The completion did not take place on 22 October, and the Plaintiff's solicitors wrote to the Defendants, intimating that the Plaintiff accepted the Defendants' wrongful repudiation of the agreements.
facts.F12: The Defendants had entered into voluntary liquidation, and the liquidators did not oppose the Plaintiff's applications.
facts.F13: The Plaintiff lawfully terminated the agreements.
facts.F14: The Plaintiff provided evidence to support the lawful termination.

requested_remedy: The applicant seeks to recover further compensation for permanent partial incapacity arising out of and in the course of his employment.
parties: Defendant: HOP HING CHEONG TIMBER YARD

facts.F1: The applicant, Leung Wing-hung, has been working for the respondent since 1975, initially as an odd-job worker and later engaging in heavy work lifting heavy weights of timber.
facts.F2: In 1983 and 1984, the applicant suffered personal injuries as a result of accidents at his work, and agreements were made with the respondent for periodical payments and compensation.
facts.F3: The applicant now seeks to recover further compensation, claiming that his injury has become more serious over time due to continuing the same work with the same employer.
facts.F4: The applicant has a long history of intermittent attacks of low back pain since 1983 and has received treatment from various medical professionals.
facts.F5: The applicant's present condition is largely due to the fact that he has remained in his present employment since 1983 doing essentially the same type of heavy work.
facts.F6: The applicant was aware of the nature of his injury at the time of the agreements in 1983 and 1985.
facts.F7: The applicant may not have appreciated the extent of his injury at the time of the agreements, but this does not entitle him to cancel the agreement.
facts.F8: The applicant's present condition is due to the continuing effects of his earlier injuries, rather than a fresh injury.
